Step.description: Step is one lesson of a tutorial: some prose, and what happens on the board.

arrow.description: Arrow draws an arrow from its first square to its second.

highlight.description: Highlight are squares (or areas) to pick out on the board.

hint.description: Hint is shown when the learner asks for one ("Need a hint?"). On a step with no move to make, it can answer a question the text asks.

illegal.description: Illegal marks the step's arrow and highlighted squares as what must not be done: drawn red, with a cross. It needs one of them, and such a step asks for no moves.

keep_playing.description: KeepPlaying offers, from this lesson on, to play the game on from where it stands against a bot ("Keep Playing"): usually on the last lesson, of a tutorial whose game is worth finishing.

name.description: Name is the lesson's name, shown after the tutorial's title above it.

pieces.description: Pieces depicts the board with just these pieces on it, for this step only: piece@square, or piece:color@square where the piece is not named after its colour, bottom first where several share a square. It need not be a position play can reach, and like Show it asks for no moves.

play.description: Play are the moves the learner is asked to make, in order, in the game's notation as the engine writes it. The page offers only these.

position.description: Position depicts a position written out as a document instead, for this step only; like Show it asks for no moves.

reply.description: Reply are the moves played for the other seats after the learner's, in order.

show.description: Show depicts another position for this step only — the end of a game, say — reached by these moves from the game's start (seeded as the tutorial is). The room's game is not touched. A step that shows a position asks for no moves.

spotlight.description: Spotlight are the parts of the game's page to pick out, by name: the player's Power, the round's phases, the History. See PageParts. A part of a player's panel means the learner's, or another seat's as doom:2.

text.description: Text is the step's prose, in Markdown (the game's guide images may be used, as in its rules pages).

Tutorial.description: Tutorial is one tutorial of a game.

game.description: Game is the game (or variant) the tutorial is played on, a member of the family whose files hold it.

id.description: ID names the tutorial; unique among the game's tutorials.

kind.description: Kind is rules, strategy or variant.

order.description: Order sorts the game's tutorials of one kind (lowest first), and so the tutorials of a series.

seat.description: Seat is the learner's seat (default 1); the page plays every other.

seed.description: Seed fixes the chance of a game that has any (its dice), so every roll of the scripted line comes out the same. Required for such a game.

series.description: Series names the ordered set of tutorials this one belongs to ("Core Game"), taken one after another in Order. Without it a tutorial is a series of its own. A series' tutorials are of one kind.

setup.description: Setup are moves played, by whichever seat is to move, before the first step: the way to reach a position worth teaching from.

start.description: Start is a position document the tutorial begins from instead of the game's start — a game well into play, which would take hundreds of moves to reach — usually kept in a file of its own with !include. The game checks it as it checks any custom start; its own state of chance is used, so no seed is needed. StartSeat is who moves first from it in a game whose position does not say (a game without a Go ruleset).

steps.description: Steps are shown one after another.

title.description: Title is what the list of tutorials shows; Summary is one line under it.

variant_only.description: VariantOnly says the tutorial teaches the game it names and no other of its family, so it is offered only with that game. Without it a tutorial is offered for the whole family, and Game is merely the board it is played on.
